learning.why: The teacher’s diagram showed the overlapping dot, and I finally saw why it’s 13 not 14.

end.summary:
Practised using dot and tile pictures to show how square patterns grow by adding a row and column; corner overlap was counted once.
Practised using a picture as an argument for the new tiles: 9 + 9 − 1 = 17, then 17 × 20 = 340 rupees; this was not steady yet.
Practised triangular patterns by adding the next row: 1, 3, 6, 10 and 21 + 7 = 28.
The 4-by-5 rectangle was identified as 20 dots, with half as 10 for the triangle; this still needs checking next time.
end.parentNote: Ishita practised showing growing square and triangular patterns with pictures. They used the shared corner rule to calculate 17 new tiles and then 340 rupees, and later applied the same idea in a repeated explanation; this was not steady yet. They also practised adding the next row in triangular patterns and identifying a 4-by-5 rectangle as 20 dots, with half as 10. At home, ask them to draw one growing square and label the new row, new column, and shared corner.
